newsitem.title: USA: Late semiconductor rally helps erase Nasdaq losses.
newsitem.headline: Late semiconductor rally helps erase Nasdaq losses.

text.p: A late-afternoon rally allowed the Nasdaq market to end a trace higher on Friday, with keen interest in semiconductor issues erasing moderate intraday losses.
The Nasdaq composite index gained 0.52 point, or 0.03 percent, to close unofficially at 1594.33. Declining issues beat advancers 11 to 10 on total volume of 593 million shares.
"The chips saved the day; people came snapping them up," one trader said, adding that Merrill Lynch had helped bolster the segment with a favorable comment about semiconductors earlier Friday.

"And PC makers were strong considering that bonds were down all day long," a trading manager said, referring to the 30-year Treasury bond which fell 2-3/32 to yield 6.46 percent compared to 6.30 percent at Thursday's close.
The bond selloff came amid release of strong economic data that fueled inflation fears.
Intel Corp rose 1-13/16 to 93-5/8. The chipmaker Friday formally launched its $17.50 per share tender offer for all the shares of Chips and Technologies Inc.
Applied Materials Inc, whose equipment is used to make semiconductors, jumped 4-21/32 to 96-17/32.
